overview: Several storm systems move through the West this week, with the Pacific Northwest and Cascades getting the most snow and rain through Thursday and Friday. The Northern Rockies and Colorado see snow Friday into Saturday. The Northeast and Canada get a mix of rain and snow late in the week.

regions.title: Cascades
regions.text: A frontal system brings wind and mixed rain and snow Wednesday night into Thursday, with snow mainly at the high passes. Crystal Mountain leads at 39" for the week, with its biggest day Thursday at 14". Winds could make Thanksgiving travel on I-5 harder, so allow extra time. A Winter Storm Watch covers Washington Pass.

regions.title: Northern Rockies
regions.text: Dry, mild weather holds through Thanksgiving. A system arrives Friday, with snow in western Wyoming through Saturday, and the snow band could shift depending on where the front stalls. Grand Targhee leads the region at 43" for the week, with its biggest day Friday at 22". Fog is likely in Jackson Hole and the Bighorn Basin Wednesday morning.

regions.title: Northeast
regions.text: Cold, dry weather holds through early Thursday. A system brings mostly rain late Thanksgiving into Friday, with a brief wintry mix at higher elevations at the start. Snow is mainly limited to mountain summits over the weekend, with a clipper-type system passing well north. Stowe and Jay Peak both peak Friday at 12" to 13".

regions.title: Coast Mountains
regions.text: Rain and showers dominate Wednesday through Friday, with a mix of sun and cloud by Saturday. Snow returns Sunday and into Sunday night at higher elevations. Whistler's biggest day is Thursday at 13".

regions.title: Tahoe
regions.text: Dry weather holds through Thanksgiving, with patchy freezing fog in the valleys. A system brings rain and high-elevation snow Sunday into Monday, with a stronger, colder storm possible Tuesday into Wednesday that could make Sierra passes difficult. Sugar Bowl leads the region with 18" on Sunday.

regions.title: Kootenays
regions.text: Rain and showers continue Wednesday through Thursday, with snow levels rising Wednesday morning. Colder air brings flurries Sunday. Whitewater's biggest day is Thursday at 7".

regions.title: Central Rockies
regions.text: Mild, dry weather holds through Thanksgiving, and Friday is the warmest day along the Front Range. Northwest flow brings snow to the Park Range Friday and Saturday, and totals are uncertain. Steamboat peaks Saturday at 11"; Vail gets 9" that day.

regions.title: Okanagan
regions.text: Showers arrive Wednesday night into Thursday, then give way to mixed sun and cloud Friday and Saturday. Snow returns Sunday night. Big White's biggest day is Thursday at 6".

sources.name: NOAA buoys 51001 / 51101 (method: Powder Buoy, Mike Ruzek)

buoy.text: Buoys 51001 and 51101 near Hawaii popped Nov 11, the swell signal Powder Buoy watches for a Wasatch storm about two weeks later — here Nov 22–28. In past winters a pop raised the chance of a Wasatch storm in that window by roughly 6 to 12 points. Experimental: promising, not proven.
